title: Andy Razaf, his first collaborator
summary: Razaf was the first person he collaborated with, a very talented lyricist whose many joint songs were never published.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now let's talk about your collaborators; you know, all the people you collaborated with -- I'd love to get in to that. And by the way, before we leave Mamie Smith and her records, you told me that you've got some of her original records, and they're jewels, and we'll get together and maybe put a couple of them on the tape when we send this to the Smithsonian. That would be nice.
All right. Now, who was the first person you collaborated with?
He was the first person I collaborated with.
All right, tell us about Andy Razaf
and what was he like, and how did you happen to get together on that first collaboration.

Well, Andy Razaf, I would say, you couldn't get a more talented person than Andy Razaf, because he wrote the song, "Ain't Misbehaving", "Honeysuckle Rose", "Supposing" and oh, so many other songs. Later on. But during his tenure and mine, we wrote an awful lot of songs together, songs that were never published, and never recorded, even. But we wrote them -- we had to have something to do, so we wrote songs.
JC, you have them around, right?
It might be pretty nice if we got together and made a few contacts and tried to get them published now, or recorded.
